title: Proper schemes of dimension at most one map finitely when no curve component is contracted
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X,Y$ be schemes over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a $k$-morphism. Suppose that $Y$ is separated over $k$ and $X$ is proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], that $\dim X\leq1$ for the topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and that for every irreducible component $Z\subseteq X$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] of dimension one the set $f(Z)$ contains at least two points. Then $f$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0CCL, lemma-finite, all three hypotheses and the conclusion

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated] over $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$. The equality of composites required there is exactly the hypothesis that $f$ is a $k$-morphism. Thus $f$ is proper. By [def-weil-proper-morphism], its underlying map is closed, so $f(X)$ is closed and $f(x)$ is closed in $Y$ whenever $x$ is closed in $X$.

source.place: Tag 0CCL (lemma-finite), first two sentences; Morphisms Tag 01W6 (lemma-image-proper-scheme-closed)

proof.text: Properness of $X$ implies finite type over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism]. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $X$ has a finite affine open cover $X=\bigcup_i\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ with each $A_i$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra. By [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components] each $A_i$ is Noetherian and each chart has Noetherian topology. Therefore $X$ is a Noetherian scheme: it is quasi-compact with a finite cover by Noetherian affine schemes. Its topology is Noetherian too: a descending chain of closed subsets stabilizes on each chart, hence globally after the maximum of the finitely many stabilization indices.

source.place: Tag 0CCL, implicit Noetherian input in the finite-fibre argument; Morphisms Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), Properties Tag 01OZ (lemma-Noetherian-topology)

proof.text: Fix a closed point $x\in X$ and put $y=f(x)$. By step 1 the fibre subset $F_y=f^{-1}(\{y\})$ is closed in $X$. We show $\dim F_y\leq0$ directly from [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. If $A\subsetneq B$ were nonempty irreducible closed subsets of $F_y$, they would also be closed in $X$. No irreducible closed subset of $X$ could strictly contain $B$, since that would give a length-two chain in $X$. Hence $B$ is an irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components]; the chain $A\subsetneq B$ and $\dim X\leq1$ give $\dim B=1$. But $B\subseteq F_y$ implies $f(B)=\{y\}$, contrary to the noncontraction hypothesis. There is thus no length-one chain in $F_y$, as required.

source.place: Tag 0CCL (lemma-finite), closed fibre avoids the dimension-one components; the dimension argument spelled out

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components] to the closed subset $F_y$ of the Noetherian scheme $X$. It is a finite union of irreducible closed subsets $C_j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober] each $C_j$ has a generic point $\xi_j$. If it contained $z\ne\xi_j$, the nonempty irreducible closed subset $\overline{\{z\}}\subseteq C_j$ would have to equal $C_j$, since step 3 rules out a strict inclusion. Then $z$ too would be a generic point of $C_j$, contradicting uniqueness. Thus $C_j=\{\xi_j\}$ and $F_y$ is finite.

source.place: Tag 0CCL (lemma-finite), sentence concluding the fibre is finite; Properties Tag 0BA8 (lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components), Schemes Tag 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober)

proof.text: For every image $y=f(x)$ of a closed point $x\in X$, steps 1 and 4 verify the hypotheses of [lem-trf-proper-finite-fibre-finite-near]. Obtain an open neighbourhood $U_y$ of $y$ such that $f^{-1}(U_y)\to U_y$ is finite. This use imposes no Noetherian or finite-type assumption on $Y$.

source.place: Tag 0CCL (lemma-finite), finite-neighbourhood conclusion using More on Morphisms Tag 02UP (lemma-proper-finite-fibre-finite-in-neighbourhood)

proof.text: Put $U=\bigcup_yU_y$, indexed by the images of closed points just considered. If $E=f^{-1}(Y\setminus U)$ were nonempty, it would be a nonempty closed subset of $X$. Since $X$ is locally of finite type over $k$, [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] says the closed points of $X$ lying in $E$ are dense in $E$, hence at least one such point $x$ exists. But then $f(x)\in U_{f(x)}\subseteq U$, contradicting $x\in E$. Thus $f(X)\subseteq U$; together with step 1 this gives the open cover $Y=U\cup(Y\setminus f(X))$.

source.place: Tag 0CCL (lemma-finite), final sentence about enough images of closed points; Varieties Tag 0478 (lemma-locally-finite-type-Jacobson)

proof.text: Refine the open cover in step 6 by affine opens contained in some $U_y$ or in $Y\setminus f(X)$. For an affine open $V\subseteq U_y$, its inverse image is affine because $f^{-1}(U_y)\to U_y$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. For $V\subseteq Y\setminus f(X)$ the inverse image is empty, hence affine ($\operatorname{Spec}$ of the zero ring). By [pqf-lem-affine-local-target] the morphism $f$ is affine. It is proper by step 1, so [lem-sfb-affine-proper-finite] implies that $f$ is finite.

source.place: Tag 0CCL (lemma-finite), locality implicit in the last sentence; Morphisms Tags 01S8 (lemma-characterize-affine) and 01WN (lemma-finite-proper)
